records.source: וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים חָמֵשׁ֩ אַמּ֨וֹת אֹ֜רֶךְ וְחָמֵ֧שׁ אַמּ֣וֹת רֹ֗חַב רָב֤וּעַ יִהְיֶה֙ הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וְשָׁלֹ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת קֹמָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And you will make the altar [of] woods of acacia, five cubits length and five cubits breadth; square will be the altar, and three cubits its height.
pieces: Make the altar out of acacia wood. It is to be square, {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|5 cubits}} on each side and {{units:about 4 1/2 feet|3 cubits}} high.

L.1: And you shall make the altar [of] acacia wood, 5 cubits [in] length and 5 cubits [in] breadth; square the altar shall be, and 3 cubits its height.

R.1: Build an altar for burnt offerings out of acacia wood. Make it square, {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|5 cubits}} on each side and {{units:about 4 1/2 feet|3 cubits}} tall.

decisions.choice: the altar: the bronze altar of burnt offering in the courtyard
decisions.reason: "The altar" is the altar for the daily burnt offerings (29:38-42), set in the courtyard before the entrance of the tabernacle (40:6, 29). It is later called the altar of burnt offering (30:28; 38:1) and the bronze altar (38:30), to tell it apart from the gold altar of incense inside (30:1-6).

decisions.choice: cubit: a measure of length, from the elbow to the tip of the fingers, about 18 inches
decisions.reason: The cubit was the common measure of length, the length of a forearm, about 18 inches (about 45 centimeters). The altar was about 7 1/2 feet square and about 4 1/2 feet high.

decisions.choice: modern measure first, cubits as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the altar's size in feet by default, with the cubits of the Hebrew as the units alternative (a cubit is about 18 inches; see the note at verse 1). Literal keeps cubits.

decisions.choice: an altar for burnt offerings
decisions.reason: Readable says what the altar is for, since this is the first time it is described (see 29:38-42; 38:1). Literal and Balanced keep "the altar".

records.heading: The altar

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ קַרְנֹתָ֗יו עַ֚ל אַרְבַּ֣ע פִּנֹּתָ֔יו מִמֶּ֖נּוּ תִּהְיֶ֣יןָ קַרְנֹתָ֑יו וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹת֖וֹ נְחֹֽשֶׁת׃
records.gloss: And you will make its horns on its four corners; from it will be its horns, and you will overlay it [with] bronze.
pieces: Shape horns on its four corners, forming part of the altar itself, and overlay it all with bronze.

L.2: And you shall make its horns on its four corners; its horns shall be from it, and you shall overlay it [with] bronze.

R.2: Make a horn-shaped point that sticks up at each of its four corners. These horns must be part of the altar itself, not separate pieces. Cover the whole altar with bronze.

decisions.choice: horns: points rising at the corners of the altar, shaped like horns
decisions.reason: The horns stood up from the four corners of the altar. The blood of the sin offering was put on them (29:12; Leviticus 4:7), and a person in danger might take hold of them to seek protection (1 Kings 1:50; 2:28).

decisions.choice: its horns shall be from it: of one piece with the altar
decisions.reason: The horns were not to be made separately and fixed on; they were part of the altar's own structure, as the lampstand's cups and branches are "from it" (25:31, 36).

decisions.choice: bronze: copper or a copper alloy
decisions.reason: The word covers copper and its alloys. Bronze marks the courtyard and its altar, while gold is used for the furnishings inside the tabernacle (25:11-39).

decisions.choice: a horn-shaped point that sticks up
decisions.reason: Readable describes the horns, which a reader may not picture, and spells out "from it" as "part of the altar itself".

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ סִּֽירֹתָיו֙ לְדַשְּׁנ֔וֹ וְיָעָיו֙ וּמִזְרְקֹתָ֔יו וּמִזְלְגֹתָ֖יו וּמַחְתֹּתָ֑יו לְכָל־כֵּלָ֖יו תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה נְחֹֽשֶׁת׃
records.gloss: And you will make its pots to take away its fatty ashes, and its shovels and its bowls and its forks and its firepans; for all its articles you will make [of] bronze.
pieces: Make its pots for clearing away the fat-soaked ashes, along with its shovels, basins, forks and firepans. All of its utensils are to be made of bronze.

L.3: And you shall make its pots for removing its fatty ashes, and its shovels and its basins and its forks and its firepans; all its utensils you shall make [of] bronze.

R.3: Make pots to carry away the greasy ashes. Also make shovels, bowls, forks, and pans for carrying hot coals. Make all these tools out of bronze.

decisions.choice: removing its fatty ashes: clearing out the ashes soaked with the fat of the offerings
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for ashes mixed with fat from the burnt offerings. These were carried out to a clean place (Leviticus 1:16; 4:12).

decisions.choice: basins: bowls for the blood of the offerings
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning to throw or splash. These bowls held the blood of the sacrifices, which was splashed against the altar (24:6; 29:16).

decisions.choice: forks ... firepans: forks for the meat, and pans for carrying burning coals
decisions.reason: Forks were used to handle the meat of the sacrifices (1 Samuel 2:13-14). The firepans carried burning coals; the same word is used for the pans in which incense was burned (Leviticus 10:1; 16:12).

decisions.choice: greasy ashes ... pans for carrying hot coals
decisions.reason: Readable describes the ashes and says what the firepans were for. Literal and Balanced keep "fatty ashes" or "fat-soaked ashes" and "firepans".

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ לּוֹ֙ מִכְבָּ֔ר מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה רֶ֣שֶׁת נְחֹ֑שֶׁת וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ עַל־הָרֶ֗שֶׁת אַרְבַּע֙ טַבְּעֹ֣ת נְחֹ֔שֶׁת עַ֖ל אַרְבַּ֥ע קְצוֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And you will make for it a grating, a work of a net [of] bronze, and you will make on the net four rings [of] bronze on its four ends.
pieces: Make for it a grating of bronze, worked as a mesh, and attach four bronze rings to the mesh at its four corners.

L.4: And you shall make for it a grating, a work of network [of] bronze, and you shall make on the network four rings [of] bronze at its four ends.

R.4: Make a bronze grate shaped like a net for the altar. Put four bronze rings on its four corners.

decisions.choice: a grating, a work of network: a lattice of bronze, placed on the lower half of the altar
alternatives: a grate inside the altar, to hold the fire
decisions.reason: The grating was a bronze lattice set under the ledge and reaching halfway up the altar (verse 5). The text does not say whether it was inside, holding the fire, or outside, around the lower part of the frame. Rings for the poles at its corners (verse 7) suggest it was on the outside.

decisions.choice: its four ends: the four corners of the grating
decisions.reason: The rings were at the corners so that poles could be passed through them to carry the altar (verse 7).

records.source: וְנָתַתָּ֣ה אֹתָ֗הּ תַּ֛חַת כַּרְכֹּ֥ב הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ מִלְּמָ֑טָּה וְהָיְתָ֣ה הָרֶ֔שֶׁת עַ֖ד חֲצִ֥י הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃
records.gloss: And you will put it under the ledge of the altar from below, and will be the net up to [the] middle of the altar.
pieces: Place the grating beneath the ledge of the altar, down below, so that the mesh reaches to the middle of the altar.

L.5: And you shall put it under the ledge of the altar, below, and the network shall be [reaching] to the middle of the altar.

R.5: Fit the grate under the ledge that runs around the altar, so that it comes up to the middle of the altar.

decisions.choice: the ledge: a rim or border around the altar, halfway up
decisions.reason: The word is found only here and in 38:4, and its meaning is not certain. It seems to have been a ledge or band around the sides of the altar, at about half its height, with the grating below it.

decisions.choice: to the middle of the altar: halfway up its height
decisions.reason: The grating rose from the bottom of the altar to its middle, about 1 1/2 cubits up.

decisions.choice: the ledge that runs around the altar
decisions.reason: Readable describes the ledge as going around the altar, the likely sense of an uncertain word (see the footnote).

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ בַדִּים֙ לַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ בַּדֵּ֖י עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֹתָ֖ם נְחֹֽשֶׁת׃
records.gloss: And you will make poles for the altar, poles of woods of acacia, and you will overlay them [with] bronze.
pieces: The altar is also to have poles: make them of acacia wood and overlay them with bronze.

L.6: And you shall make poles for the altar, poles of acacia wood, and you shall overlay them [with] bronze.

R.6: Make poles out of acacia wood for carrying the altar, and cover them with bronze.

decisions.choice: poles: carrying poles
decisions.reason: Like the ark and the table (25:13-15, 27-28), the altar was carried on poles when Israel moved camp (Numbers 4:13-14).

decisions.choice: for carrying the altar
decisions.reason: Readable says what the poles were for, as verse 7 makes clear.

records.source: וְהוּבָ֥א אֶת־בַּדָּ֖יו בַּטַּבָּעֹ֑ת וְהָי֣וּ הַבַּדִּ֗ים עַל־שְׁתֵּ֛י צַלְעֹ֥ת הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ בִּשְׂאֵ֥ת אֹתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And will be put its poles into the rings, and will be the poles on [the] two sides of the altar in carrying it.
pieces: The poles are to be slid through the rings, so that they run along both sides of the altar whenever it is carried.

L.7: And its poles shall be put into the rings, and the poles shall be on the two sides of the altar in carrying it.

R.7: Slide the poles through the rings. The poles will be on both sides of the altar, so people can carry it.

decisions.choice: the rings: the four rings at the corners of the grating
decisions.reason: These are the rings of verse 4. Two poles passed through them, one along each side of the altar.

decisions.choice: in carrying it: whenever the altar is moved
decisions.reason: The poles were for carrying the altar when the camp moved on (Numbers 4:13-15).

records.source: נְב֥וּב לֻחֹ֖ת תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֹת֑וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר הֶרְאָ֥ה אֹתְךָ֛ בָּהָ֖ר כֵּ֥ן יַעֲשֽׂוּ׃ס
records.gloss: Hollow of boards you will make it; just as he showed you on the mountain, so they will make [it].
pieces: The altar is to be a hollow box built of planks. Let them make it according to what you were shown on the mountain.

L.8: Hollow, [of] boards you shall make it; just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} showed you on the mountain, so they shall make [it].

R.8: Make the altar like a hollow box out of boards. The workers must build it exactly the way you were shown on the mountain.

decisions.choice: hollow, of boards: a hollow frame of planks
decisions.reason: The altar was a box of acacia planks covered with bronze, with no top or bottom. It may have been filled with earth or stones where it stood, as the earlier law of the altar asks for an altar of earth or uncut stones (20:24-25), but the text does not say so.

decisions.choice: as he showed you: as you were shown, by God
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject and may be impersonal ("as it was shown you"). God is the one who showed Moses the pattern on the mountain (25:9, 40; 26:30).

decisions.choice: you were shown
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the passive, as in 25:40 and 26:30. Readable names the workers as "they". Literal keeps "he showed you".

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֕יתָ אֵ֖ת חֲצַ֣ר הַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן לִפְאַ֣ת נֶֽגֶב־תֵּ֠ימָנָה קְלָעִ֨ים לֶחָצֵ֜ר שֵׁ֣שׁ מָשְׁזָ֗ר מֵאָ֤ה בָֽאַמָּה֙ אֹ֔רֶךְ לַפֵּאָ֖ה הָאֶחָֽת׃
records.gloss: And you will make the courtyard of the tabernacle; for the side of the south, southward, hangings for the courtyard [of] fine linen twisted, one hundred by the cubit [the] length for the one side.
pieces: You are also to make the courtyard of the tabernacle. On the south side the courtyard is to have hangings of fine twisted linen, {{units:about 150 feet|100 cubits}} long on that one side.

L.9: And you shall make the courtyard of the tabernacle. For the south side, southward, [there shall be] hangings for the courtyard [of] fine twisted linen, 100 cubits [the] length for the one side.

R.9: Make a courtyard around the tabernacle. Along the south side, put up hangings made of fine twisted linen. That side is to be {{units:about 150 feet|100 cubits}} long.

decisions.choice: hangings: lengths of cloth hung from pillars to make the courtyard wall
decisions.reason: The word is not the one used for the curtains of the tabernacle itself (26:1-13). These hangings, 5 cubits high (verse 18), formed an open-air enclosure around the tabernacle.

decisions.choice: the south side, southward: the side facing south
decisions.reason: Two words for south stand together for emphasis; the first is the name of the dry land to the south of Canaan. Each side of the courtyard is named by the direction it faces (verses 11-13).

decisions.choice: fine twisted linen: linen of fine thread, spun from several strands
decisions.reason: As in 26:1, the linen is fine, white cloth woven from thread made of strands twisted together for strength.

decisions.choice: modern measure first, cubits as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the length of the side in feet by default, with the cubits of the Hebrew as the units alternative (a cubit is about 18 inches; see the note at verse 1). Literal keeps cubits.

decisions.choice: around the tabernacle
decisions.reason: Readable says where the courtyard is; its walls went around the tabernacle on all four sides (verses 9-13).

records.heading: The courtyard

records.source: וְעַמֻּדָ֣יו עֶשְׂרִ֔ים וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֥ם עֶשְׂרִ֖ים נְחֹ֑שֶׁת וָוֵ֧י הָעַמֻּדִ֛ים וַחֲשֻׁקֵיהֶ֖ם כָּֽסֶף׃
records.gloss: And its pillars twenty and their bases twenty [of] bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands [of] silver.
pieces: Its twenty pillars are to stand in twenty bronze bases, and the hooks and bands on the pillars are to be silver.

L.10: And its pillars [shall be] twenty and their bases twenty, [of] bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands [shall be of] silver.

R.10: Hang the hangings on twenty posts that stand in twenty bronze bases. Put silver hooks and silver bands on the posts.

decisions.choice: bases: heavy sockets or stands into which the pillars were set
decisions.reason: The same word is used for the silver bases of the tabernacle frames (26:19). Here, in the courtyard, they are bronze.

decisions.choice: hooks ... bands: hooks for hanging the hangings, and bands of silver around or between the pillars
decisions.reason: The hooks held the hangings (26:32). The word for "bands" is less certain: it may mean rings around the tops of the pillars, or rods running from pillar to pillar. The related verb in verse 17 says the pillars were "banded" with silver (38:17, 28).

decisions.choice: posts
decisions.reason: Readable says "posts" for the pillars of the courtyard, which held up cloth walls rather than a roof. Literal and Balanced keep "pillars".

records.source: וְכֵ֨ן לִפְאַ֤ת צָפוֹן֙ בָּאֹ֔רֶךְ קְלָעִ֖ים מֵ֣אָה אֹ֑רֶךְ וְעַמּוּדָ֣יו עֶשְׂרִ֗ים וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֤ם עֶשְׂרִים֙ נְחֹ֔שֶׁת וָוֵ֧י הָֽעַמֻּדִ֛ים וַחֲשֻׁקֵיהֶ֖ם כָּֽסֶף׃
records.gloss: And so for the side of the north in length, hangings one hundred [cubits] length, and its pillars twenty and their bases twenty [of] bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands [of] silver.
pieces: The north side is to be the same: hangings {{units:about 150 feet|100 cubits}} long, with twenty pillars in twenty bronze bases, and silver hooks and bands on the pillars.

L.11: And likewise for the north side, in length, hangings 100 [cubits] long, and its pillars twenty and their bases twenty, [of] bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands [of] silver.

R.11: Do the same on the north side. Put up hangings {{units:about 150 feet|100 cubits}} long on twenty posts that stand in twenty bronze bases. Put silver hooks and bands on the posts.

decisions.choice: likewise ... one hundred: the north side matches the south side
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "one hundred"; the unit, cubits, is carried over from verse 9. The long north and south sides are the same in every detail.

decisions.choice: modern measure first, cubits as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the length of the side in feet by default, with the cubits of the Hebrew as the units alternative (a cubit is about 18 inches; see the note at verse 1). Literal keeps cubits.

records.source: וְרֹ֤חַב הֶֽחָצֵר֙ לִפְאַת־יָ֔ם קְלָעִ֖ים חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים אַמָּ֑ה עַמֻּדֵיהֶ֣ם עֲשָׂרָ֔ה וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֖ם עֲשָׂרָֽה׃
records.gloss: And the breadth of the courtyard for the side of [the] west, hangings [of] fifty cubits; their pillars ten and their bases ten.
pieces: Across the width of the courtyard, on the west side, there are to be hangings {{units:about 75 feet|50 cubits}} long, with ten pillars and ten bases.

L.12: And the breadth of the courtyard on the west side [shall be] hangings of 50 cubits; their pillars ten and their bases ten.

R.12: The west end of the courtyard is to be {{units:about 75 feet|50 cubits}} wide. Put up hangings there on ten posts that stand in ten bases.

decisions.choice: the west side: literally, the side of the sea
decisions.reason: In the land of Israel the Mediterranean Sea lies to the west, so "sea" is a common word for west (26:22, 27).

decisions.choice: the breadth: the short ends of the courtyard
decisions.reason: The courtyard was 100 cubits long from east to west and 50 cubits wide (verse 18). The west end lay behind the tabernacle (26:22).

decisions.choice: modern measure first, cubits as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the width of the courtyard in feet by default, with the cubits of the Hebrew as the units alternative (a cubit is about 18 inches; see the note at verse 1). Literal keeps cubits.

records.source: וְרֹ֣חַב הֶֽחָצֵ֗ר לִפְאַ֛ת קֵ֥דְמָה מִזְרָ֖חָה חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אַמָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And the breadth of the courtyard for the side of eastward, toward the sunrise, fifty cubits.
pieces: The width of the courtyard on the east side, toward the sunrise, is also to be {{units:about 75 feet|50 cubits}}.

L.13: And the breadth of the courtyard on the east side, toward the sunrise, [shall be] 50 cubits.

R.13: The east end, facing the sunrise, is also to be {{units:about 75 feet|50 cubits}} wide.

decisions.choice: the east side, toward the sunrise: the front of the courtyard
decisions.reason: Two words for east stand together, the second meaning "the place of sunrise". The courtyard and the tabernacle faced east, and the gate was on this side (verses 14-16).

decisions.choice: modern measure first, cubits as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the width of the courtyard in feet by default, with the cubits of the Hebrew as the units alternative (a cubit is about 18 inches; see the note at verse 1). Literal keeps cubits.

records.source: וַחֲמֵ֨שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה אַמָּ֛ה קְלָעִ֖ים לַכָּתֵ֑ף עַמֻּדֵיהֶ֣ם שְׁלֹשָׁ֔ה וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֖ם שְׁלֹשָֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And fifteen cubits [of] hangings for the side; their pillars three and their bases three.
pieces: On one side of the entrance there are to be hangings {{units:about 22 1/2 feet|15 cubits}} long, with three pillars and three bases.

L.14: And 15 cubits [of] hangings for the [one] side; their pillars three and their bases three.

R.14: On one side of the gate, put up hangings {{units:about 22 1/2 feet|15 cubits}} long on three posts that stand in three bases.

decisions.choice: side: literally "shoulder", the part of the east wall on either side of the gate
decisions.reason: The east end, 50 cubits wide, had 15 cubits of hangings on each side and a gateway 20 cubits wide in the middle (verses 13-16).

decisions.choice: modern measure first, cubits as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the length of the hangings in feet by default, with the cubits of the Hebrew as the units alternative (a cubit is about 18 inches; see the note at verse 1). Literal keeps cubits.

decisions.choice: of the entrance / of the gate
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say which side is meant: one side of the gateway in the east wall.

records.source: וְלַכָּתֵף֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔ית חְמֵ֥שׁעֶשְׂרֵ֖ה קְלָעִ֑ים עַמֻּדֵיהֶ֣ם שְׁלֹשָׁ֔ה וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֖ם שְׁלֹשָֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And for the second side fifteen [cubits of] hangings; their pillars three and their bases three.
pieces: On the other side there are to be hangings {{units:about 22 1/2 feet|15 cubits}} long, with three pillars and three bases.

L.15: And for the second side, 15 [cubits of] hangings; their pillars three and their bases three.

R.15: Do the same on the other side of the gate: hangings {{units:about 22 1/2 feet|15 cubits}} long on three posts that stand in three bases.

decisions.choice: the second side: the other side of the gate
decisions.reason: The two sides of 15 cubits each and the gate of 20 cubits make up the 50 cubits of the east end (verse 13). "Cubits" is carried over from verse 14.

decisions.choice: modern measure first, cubits as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the length of the hangings in feet by default, with the cubits of the Hebrew as the units alternative (a cubit is about 18 inches; see the note at verse 1). Literal keeps cubits.

records.source: וּלְשַׁ֨עַר הֶֽחָצֵ֜ר מָסָ֣ךְ׀עֶשְׂרִ֣ים אַמָּ֗ה תְּכֵ֨לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֜ן וְתוֹלַ֧עַת שָׁנִ֛י וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מָשְׁזָ֖ר מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה רֹקֵ֑ם עַמֻּֽדֵיהֶם֙ אַרְבָּעָ֔ה וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֖ם אַרְבָּעָֽה׃
records.gloss: And for the gate of the courtyard a screen [of] twenty cubits, [of] violet and purple and scarlet of crimson and fine linen twisted, [the] work of an embroiderer; their pillars four and their bases four.
pieces: The gateway of the courtyard is to have a screen {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}} wide, of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, worked by an embroiderer, and hung on four pillars set in four bases.

L.16: And for the gate of the courtyard [there shall be] a screen of 20 cubits, [of] blue and purple and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer; their pillars four and their bases four.

R.16: For the gate of the courtyard, make a screen {{units:about 30 feet|20 cubits}} wide. Have a skilled worker make it in colorful patterns, using blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen. Hang it on four posts that stand in four bases.

decisions.choice: a screen: the hanging that closed the entrance
decisions.reason: The same word is used for the screen at the door of the tabernacle (26:36-37). Unlike the white linen walls, the gate's screen was made in colors, like the tabernacle's own curtains.

decisions.choice: blue and purple and scarlet: yarn dyed in costly colors
decisions.reason: As in 25:4 and 26:1, these are wool yarns dyed blue (a blue-violet), purple and scarlet, colors that were costly to make.

decisions.choice: the work of an embroiderer: work in colored thread
alternatives: the work of a weaver in colors
decisions.reason: The word describes a worker in colors. Whether the designs were sewn on with a needle or woven into the cloth is not certain (26:36; 35:35).

decisions.choice: modern measure first, cubits as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the width of the gate in feet by default, with the cubits of the Hebrew as the units alternative (a cubit is about 18 inches; see the note at verse 1). Literal keeps cubits.

decisions.choice: a skilled worker ... in colorful patterns
decisions.reason: Readable describes the work without deciding between needlework and weaving.

records.source: כָּל־עַמּוּדֵ֨י הֶֽחָצֵ֤ר סָבִיב֙ מְחֻשָּׁקִ֣ים כֶּ֔סֶף וָוֵיהֶ֖ם כָּ֑סֶף וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֖ם נְחֹֽשֶׁת׃
records.gloss: All the pillars of the courtyard all around [will be] banded [with] silver; their hooks [of] silver and their bases [of] bronze.
pieces: Every pillar around the courtyard is to be fitted with silver bands; their hooks are to be silver and their bases bronze.

L.17: All the pillars of the courtyard all around [shall be] banded [with] silver; their hooks [of] silver and their bases [of] bronze.

R.17: All the way around the courtyard, each post is to have bands and hooks of silver and a base of bronze.

decisions.choice: banded with silver: fitted with silver bands
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the same root as "bands" in verse 10. Whether the bands ringed each pillar or joined the pillars together is not certain (see the note at verse 10; 38:17).

decisions.choice: all around: on all four sides
decisions.reason: The rule covers every pillar of the courtyard, on the long sides, the west end and the east end with its gate.

records.source: אֹ֣רֶךְ הֶֽחָצֵר֩ מֵאָ֨ה בָֽאַמָּ֜ה וְרֹ֣חַב׀חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים בַּחֲמִשִּׁ֗ים וְקֹמָ֛ה חָמֵ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת שֵׁ֣שׁ מָשְׁזָ֑ר וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֖ם נְחֹֽשֶׁת׃
records.gloss: The length of the courtyard one hundred by the cubit, and the breadth fifty by fifty, and the height five cubits, [of] fine linen twisted, and their bases [of] bronze.
pieces: In all, the courtyard measures {{units:about 150 feet|100 cubits}} in length and {{units:about 75 feet|50 cubits}} across at each end. Its walls of fine twisted linen stand {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|5 cubits}} high, and the bases are bronze.

L.18: The length of the courtyard [shall be] 100 cubits, and the breadth 50 by 50, and the height 5 cubits, [of] fine twisted linen, and their bases [of] bronze.

R.18: So the whole courtyard will be {{units:about 150 feet|100 cubits}} long and {{units:about 75 feet|50 cubits}} wide. Its linen walls will be {{units:about 7 1/2 feet|5 cubits}} high, standing in bronze bases.

decisions.choice: 50 by 50: 50 cubits at each end
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely means that the width was 50 cubits at both the west end and the east end (verses 12-13).

decisions.choice: the height 5 cubits: the height of the hangings
decisions.reason: The linen walls were 5 cubits high, half the height of the frames of the tabernacle, which were 10 cubits (26:16).

decisions.choice: modern measure first, cubits as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the size of the courtyard in feet by default, with the cubits of the Hebrew as the units alternative (a cubit is about 18 inches; see the note at verse 1). Literal keeps cubits.

decisions.choice: walls of fine twisted linen / linen walls
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "fine twisted linen", meaning the hangings. Balanced and Readable call them walls, which is what they formed.

records.source: לְכֹל֙ כְּלֵ֣י הַמִּשְׁכָּ֔ן בְּכֹ֖ל עֲבֹדָת֑וֹ וְכָל־יְתֵדֹתָ֛יו וְכָל־יִתְדֹ֥ת הֶחָצֵ֖ר נְחֹֽשֶׁת׃ס
records.gloss: For all the articles of the tabernacle in all its service, and all its tent pegs and all the pegs of the courtyard, [of] bronze.
pieces: All the tools used for every task in the tabernacle, and all its tent pegs and those of the courtyard, are to be made of bronze.

L.19: All the utensils of the tabernacle in all its service, and all its tent pegs, and all the tent pegs of the courtyard, [shall be of] bronze.

R.19: All the tools used for the work of the tabernacle must be made of bronze. So must all the tent pegs for the tabernacle and for the courtyard.

decisions.choice: the utensils of the tabernacle in all its service: the tools for setting up and working in the tabernacle
decisions.reason: These are not the gold furnishings inside the tabernacle (25:11-39) but the tools used to set it up, take it down and serve in it, which were bronze like the courtyard.

decisions.choice: tent pegs: pegs driven into the ground to hold the cords
decisions.reason: The pegs held down the cords of the tabernacle and of the courtyard hangings (35:18; 38:20, 31).

records.source: וְאַתָּ֞ה תְּצַוֶּ֣ה׀אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְיִקְח֨וּ אֵלֶ֜יךָ שֶׁ֣מֶן זַ֥יִת זָ֛ךְ כָּתִ֖ית לַמָּא֑וֹר לְהַעֲלֹ֥ת נֵ֖ר תָּמִֽיד׃
records.gloss: And you, you will command the sons of Israel, and they will bring to you oil of olive, pure, beaten, for the light, to cause to go up a lamp continually.
pieces: You are to give the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} this command: they must bring you pure beaten olive oil for the light, to make a lamp burn continually.

L.20: And you, you shall command the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel that they bring to you pure olive oil, beaten, for the light, to make a lamp burn continually.

R.20: Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to bring you pure olive oil, made from crushed olives, for the light. That way a lamp can be kept burning all the time.

decisions.choice: pure beaten olive oil: the finest oil, from olives crushed by hand
decisions.reason: Beaten oil came from olives crushed in a mortar rather than pressed, which gave the clearest oil, used here for the lamp and in the daily offering (29:40; 1 Kings 5:11). The same command is repeated in Leviticus 24:2-4.

decisions.choice: to make a lamp burn: literally, to make a lamp go up
decisions.reason: The verb "to make go up" is used for lighting lamps (25:37; 30:8), perhaps because the flame rises. "Lamp" may stand for the lamps of the lampstand together (25:37).

decisions.choice: continually: regularly, every night
decisions.reason: The lamp was to burn through each night, "from evening to morning" (verse 21; 30:7-8; 1 Samuel 3:3), not without ever going out.

decisions.choice: made from crushed olives ... all the time
decisions.reason: Readable explains "beaten" and says "all the time" for "continually"; the note explains that this means every night.

records.heading: Oil for the lamp

records.source: בְּאֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵד֩ מִח֨וּץ לַפָּרֹ֜כֶת אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־הָעֵדֻ֗ת יַעֲרֹךְ֩ אֹת֨וֹ אַהֲרֹ֧ן וּבָנָ֛יו מֵעֶ֥רֶב עַד־בֹּ֖קֶר לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה חֻקַּ֤ת עוֹלָם֙ לְדֹ֣רֹתָ֔ם מֵאֵ֖ת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: In [the] tent of meeting, outside the curtain which [is] over the testimony, will arrange it Aaron and his sons from evening until morning before Yahweh; a statute of perpetuity for their generations from the sons of Israel.
pieces: Aaron and his sons are to tend it in the tent of meeting, outside the curtain that screens the testimony, from evening to morning before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. This is a statute for all time for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, generation after generation.

L.21: In the tent of meeting, outside the veil which [is] over the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall arrange it from evening until morning before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; [it is] a statute forever throughout their generations from the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.

R.21: Aaron and his sons must take care of the lamp in the tent of meeting, outside the curtain in front of the ark that held the covenant tablets. They must keep it burning before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from evening until morning. This is a rule the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} must keep for all time, in every generation.

decisions.choice: the tent of meeting: the tent where God meets with his people
decisions.reason: This is the first use of the name in Exodus. God says he will meet with Moses and the Israelites there (29:42-43; 33:7). It is another name for the tabernacle.

decisions.choice: the veil over the testimony: the inner curtain in front of the ark
decisions.reason: The veil of 26:31-33 divided the holy place from the most holy place, where the ark held the testimony, the tablets of the covenant (25:16, 21). The lampstand stood outside it, in the holy place (26:35).

decisions.choice: a statute forever ... from the sons of Israel: a lasting duty laid on Israel
alternatives: to be supplied by the sons of Israel
decisions.reason: The tending of the lamp is a statute for all generations. "From the sons of Israel" may mean that the duty is required of Israel, or that the oil for it is to come from them (verse 20).

decisions.choice: tend / take care of
decisions.reason: The verb means to set in order; for a lamp, to trim it and fill it so it keeps burning. Literal keeps "arrange".

decisions.choice: curtain
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "curtain" for the inner veil, as in 26:31-35. Literal keeps "veil".

decisions.choice: the ark that held the covenant tablets ... a rule
decisions.reason: Readable names the ark that held the testimony, the covenant tablets, and says "rule" for "statute". Balanced says "statute for all time"; Literal "statute forever".
